title: When the Horizon Sings
premise: When a government survey team vanishes on the Serpent's Reach, riverboat captain Paloma Fairweather is hired—coerced, really—to run the rescue, only to discover the team didn't disappear: they fled from what they found in the flooded caves upstream. Paloma and her ragtag crew must decide whether the discovery belongs to the government that hid it, the river people it endangers, or no one at all. As the monsoon closes in and the survey's sole survivor turns hunter, Paloma chooses truth over loyalty, broadcasting the finding before the waters rise—and pays for it with her boat, her reputation, and nearly her life.
about_author: Hazel Ishikawa spent six years working seasonal river transport in Southeast Asia before turning to fiction, a period she credits for her obsession with water, weather, and the lies people tell to survive both. She writes from a houseboat she refuses to name publicly.

chapters.title: The River Keeps Its Receipts
chapters.summary: Paloma Fairweather pilots the Magpie Jay through low-water season, establishing her intimate knowledge of the Reach and her crew: engineer Bao, deckhand Suri, and cook-turned-navigator Old Wen. A government courier offers triple pay for an emergency charter. POV: Paloma. Beat: restless competence shadowed by debt—the hook of easy money.

chapters.title: Paper with Teeth
chapters.summary: Paloma reads the contract: salvage and rescue of the survey vessel Kestrel, absolute secrecy clauses, penalties that would ruin her. Bao warns it smells wrong; Suri needs the money for her mother's clinic. They sign. POV: Paloma. Beat: uneasy commitment, loyalty already straining against instinct.

chapters.title: Upstream of Silence
chapters.summary: The Magpie Jay passes abandoned fishing camps and villages gone quiet. Old Wen notes the birds are missing from stretches where they always gather. First signs the river itself is avoiding something. POV: Suri. Beat: creeping dread replacing adventure.

chapters.title: Gear Without Ghosts
chapters.summary: They find the Kestrel moored intact—supplies stacked, engines cold, no bodies, no tracks in the mud except leading into the water. Paloma realizes the team left deliberately and quietly. POV: Paloma. Beat: the mystery sharpens from accident to choice.

chapters.title: What the Caves Swallowed
chapters.summary: Following a torn map fragment, they locate the cave system the survey targeted: flooded chambers humming with something seismic and strange—water that moves against current. Suri falls ill after contact. POV: Suri. Beat: wonder curdling into fear.

chapters.title: The Survivor Who Isn't Grateful
chapters.summary: They find Dr. Elias Voss, the survey's geologist, half-starved but armed. He begs them to turn back and refuses to say why, then tries to sabotage their radio. POV: Bao. Beat: distrust; Voss is either mad or protecting them.

chapters.title: Monsoon Math
chapters.summary: Old Wen calculates they have nine days before the monsoon seals the upper Reach. The government's check-in schedule gives them less. Paloma must choose: push deeper or retreat with nothing. POV: Paloma. Beat: pressure mounts, clock established.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Currency
chapters.summary: A second government boat appears—security contractor Renn and his men, ostensibly reinforcements. Paloma recognizes enforcement when she sees it. Voss whispers to her: 'They're not here to rescue anyone.' POV: Bao. Beat: allies revealed as wardens.

chapters.title: Suri's Fever Dream
chapters.summary: Delirious, Suri describes what she touched in the caves—a living network in the water, ancient and communicative. Her fever breaks with impossible knowledge of the river's channels. POV: Suri. Beat: the discovery becomes personal, not abstract.

chapters.title: The Kestrel's Logbook
chapters.summary: Bao cracks the survey's sealed log: the team found a subterranean aquifer system the government plans to dam and divert—drowning every settlement downstream. The team didn't vanish; they scattered to stop it. POV: Bao. Beat: the moral stakes crystallize.

chapters.title: Renn's Offer
chapters.summary: Renn privately offers Paloma a fortune to deliver Voss and the logbook downstream and forget the rest. He makes clear refusal means the Magpie Jay becomes 'salvage.' POV: Paloma. Beat: temptation priced against conscience.

chapters.title: Old Wen's Crossing
chapters.summary: Renn's men try to seize the logbook; in the scuffle Old Wen takes a bullet shielding Suri and dies at the wheel he loved. Paloma hides the body's loss from Renn while grief hardens into resolve. POV: Paloma. Beat: first blood—the price of survival begins.

chapters.title: Running Dark
chapters.summary: Paloma runs the boat engineless through night fog using Suri's fever-given knowledge of hidden channels, evading Renn's patrol boat. A near-fatal passage through a rock throat bonds crew and Voss at last. POV: Suri. Beat: trust forged under fire.

chapters.title: Voss Confesses
chapters.summary: Voss admits he signed off on the diversion plan until he saw the aquifer was alive—part of a watershed ecosystem older than any nation's claim. He scattered his own team to buy time. POV: Bao. Beat: antagonist reframed as witness; truth fully surfaced.

chapters.title: The Reach Answers
chapters.summary: In the deep caves, the water responds to Suri—currents parting, showing them a dry route to the relay tower on the ridge. The river isn't just scenery; it's choosing sides. POV: Suri. Beat: awe; the theme of identity—who do we owe—made literal.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Tower
chapters.summary: At the relay tower they find one of Voss's scattered teammates has already sold them out to Renn. Ambushed, Bao is captured; Paloma escapes with the logbook pages but loses the boat. POV: Paloma. Beat: lowest point—crew broken, evidence at risk.

chapters.title: Two Days of Rain
chapters.summary: Monsoon arrives early. Paloma and Voss trek through flooding jungle toward the coastal transmitter while Suri, captive aboard the Magpie Jay, stalls Renn by feeding him false channels. POV: Suri. Beat: endurance; each character paying separately for the same truth.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: At the transmitter, Paloma sends the full survey record—diversion plans, the living aquifer, the drowned villages it would create—to every port authority and newsroom on the coast. Renn arrives mid-transmission. POV: Paloma. Beat: climax; truth chosen over safety.

chapters.title: What the Water Takes
chapters.summary: Renn tries to destroy the tower; the flood-swollen river undermines its foundation, and in the collapse Renn drowns pursuing the last logbook page. Paloma nearly follows, saved by Suri arriving in the recovered Magpie Jay. POV: Paloma. Beat: catharsis—the wilderness forgives nothing, but it settles accounts.

chapters.title: Aftermath in High Water
chapters.summary: Downstream, the broadcast detonates: injunctions filed, the diversion frozen pending review, Voss testifying. The government disavows Renn. Paloma faces charges for the stolen charter but the crew's testimony holds. POV: Bao. Beat: justice partial and costly, but real.

chapters.title: The Price Itemized
chapters.summary: Paloma buries Old Wen at the confluence he loved. Suri's mother's clinic is funded by anonymous donations she suspects come from Voss. The Magpie Jay needs a new engine they can't afford. POV: Suri. Beat: mourning and accounting—survival's bill comes due.

chapters.title: When the Horizon Sings
chapters.summary: Months later, running charters again on a patched boat, Paloma hears the low harmonic hum from the caves carry across open water at dawn—the river singing what it knows. She doesn't tell anyone. Some truths belong to the water now. POV: Paloma. Beat: quiet resolution; identity remade around what was survived.
